 Hon'Ble Madan Pal Singh, J. 
1.
List has been revised.
2. None is present on behalf of the revisionist, whereas Shri Sarvajeet Singh, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned A.G.A. appearing for the State-opposite party no.1 are present.

3. Since none appeared on behalf of the revisionist even in the revised call, this Court has left with no option but to decide the instant criminal revision with the assistance of learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 as well as learned AGA and the material available on record.

4. The present criminal revision has been preferred with the prayer to set aside the order dated 24.01.2024 passed by the Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Budaun in Criminal Misc. Case No. 11 of 2022 (Deepyanti Vs. Sandeep) filed under Section 125 Cr.P.C Police Station- Bajirganj,
District- Budaun, by which the application of the opposite party no.2 filed under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
has been partly allowed and the revisionist was directed to pay Rs.5,000/- per month as maintenance to the opposite party no.2 from the date of application.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 states that the opposite party no.2 was being tortured at the matrimonial house and she was subjected to cruelty in the form of demand of additional dowry that is why the opposite party no.2 is living separately from the revisionist.

6. The learned trial court has framed issue no.1, which was decided in favour of the opposite party no.2 and against the revisionist wherein detailed reasoning has been given regarding separate living of the opposite party no.2.
Since the findings recorded by the trial court is a finding of fact, this Court being the revisional deems it appropriate not to interfere with the findings of fact recorded by the trial court.

The revisional jurisdiction of this Court is very limited, unless the findings recorded by the trial court is completely perverse or against the fact and law, the revisional court should refrain itself from interference in the findings of fact recorded by the trial court.

7. From the perusal of the judgment of the trial court, it reflects that the opposite party no.2 was harassed at her matrimonial house and the revisionist and his family members had demanded Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs) in cash and on account of that Case Crime No.09 of 2023,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, was also registered against the revisionist, therefore, the findings of the trial court regarding separate living is sufficient and satisfactory.

8. So far as income of the revisionist is concerned, learned trial court at page no.9 of the judgment finds that the revisionist has sufficient means, he has agricultural land and further the revisionist earns Rs.7,778/- per month as Rojgar Sewak, therefore, the trial court has reached at the conclusion that the revisionist is a wealthy person and having sufficient means to maintain the opposite party no.2.
Apart from this, it is the pious duty of the revisionist and further it is legal obligation on the part of the revisionist to maintain his wife and children.

There is nothing on record to show that the opposite party no.2 has any source of income, therefore, the amount of maintenance of Rs.5,000/-

2 per month granted in favour of the opposite party no.2 keeping in view the inflation rate and cost of living cannot be said to be excessive.

sentences.text: 9. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 as well as learned AGA, this Court of the considered view that it is admitted case that the opposite party no.2 is the legally wedded wife of the revisionist.

The trial court while deciding the application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. of the opposite party no.2 has framed as many as three issues and a categorical findings of fact have been recorded on each issues.

Therefore, this Court being the Revisional Court, cannot re-appreciate the evidence and also substitute its own finding in place of findings of fact recorded by the trial court on the issue in question unless the finding is completely perverse and against the facts and law.
Accordingly, the instant revision lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.
10. In view of above, the instant criminal revision being bereft of merit is dismissed.

(Madan Pal Singh,J.) October 6, 2025 Prajapati RK  Sandeep vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139011917/
